chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Prayer in congregation surpasses every individual prayer by twenty-four degrees, making it twenty-five prayers."
And from him, from an-Nadr from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him saying:

"The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Fajr, then turned his face to his companions and asked about some people, naming them by name, saying, 'Did they attend the prayer?' They said, 'No, O Messenger of God.' He said, 'Are they absent?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'Indeed, there is no prayer more burdensome for the hypocrites than this prayer and the 'Isha prayer. If they knew what merit is in them, they would come to them even if they had to crawl.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward difference between congregational prayer and individual prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quantifies the spiritual merit of congregational prayer as twenty-four degrees above individual prayer, a metric often interpreted as the cumulative reward for the individual prayer plus the collective bonus. The second part highlights the strategic significance of Fajr and 'Isha prayers, noting their particular difficulty for hypocrites (munafiqun) due to the darkness and effort required, thereby serving as a litmus test for sincere devotion. This emphasis on the communal aspect of worship reinforces the Shia understanding of unity (jamāʿah) as a source of spiritual strength and divine favor.
